text:
Alex Turner: Heads up — spotted a potential leak with the Python SDK stream iterator. When cancelling mid-stream the TCP connection lingers and file descriptors pile up. Repro below.

Priya Nair: ouch. can you paste the minimal repro?

Alex Turner: sure. synchronous client, chunked streaming:
```python
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD'))
iter = client.stream_text(model='gpt-4x', prompt='long')
next(iter)  # get first chunk
# simulate cancel from app
iter.close()
# connection remains ESTABLISHED on linux for a long time
```
This also happens if we let the iterator go out of scope without calling close().

Sam Chen: does async behave the same? like `async for chunk in client.astream_text(...)` + cancel?

Alex Turner: interestingly async path is different. `async for` does trigger `aclose()` on cancellation in our tests, but the sync generator's `close()` isn't implemented consistently. I can repro with uvloop too (WS/HTTP chunked).

Diego Ramos: any error/stacktrace when you call close()?

Alex Turner: no error. The generator stops yielding but underlying requests.Session/socket isn't closed because our wrapper relies on GC finalizers to cleanup. Garbage collection delays = leak.

Priya Nair: we should never rely on GC. SDK should offer explicit context manager + a close method that reliably terminates transport.

Sam Chen: agree. propose: implement __enter__/__exit__ and __iter__/__next__ wrapper that proxies to a StreamingResponse object with a .close() that calls transport.close() synchronously. Also add __del__ as last resort.

Alex Turner: patch idea: 1) expose context manager: `with client.stream_text(...) as stream:` 2) stream.close() calls response.raw.close() / session.close() depending on transport. 3) add unit test that asserts FD count stable after repeated start/stop.

CI Bot: Build queued — label: devex/needs-triage.

Priya Nair: this should be P1 for 0.9.x. It causes customer service tickets for long-lived apps. Also impacts on-prem (<-> load) because leaked sockets exhaust ports.

Diego Ramos: quick workaround for users: use `with` or explicitly call `client._transport.shutdown()` (internal) but warn it's not public API. We should provide official public API soon.

Sam Chen: can someone open a PR with tests? I can review. Also add typing for the stream return type: `Iterator[StreamingChunk]` and `AsyncIterator[StreamingChunk]` so mypy knows close/aclclose exists.

Alex Turner: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/432 — implements context manager + close + tests. still needs typing fixes and docs.

Priya Nair: good. add a short note in changelog and a snippet in quickstart showing proper cancellation pattern. Many users assume generator auto-closes.

Sam Chen: also add a small integration test that runs `psutil.Process().num_fds()` before/after loop to detect fd leaks — flaky on some CI runners but valuable locally.

Diego Ramos: will backport to 0.8.x branch after PR is merged. assign to eng-ml for review if it touches transport.

Alex Turner: thank you. logging TODO: emit a warning when generator is GC-collected without being closed (so devs see it).

Priya Nair: created internal ticket: DX-789. tagging @oncall for awareness. :eyes:

Sam Chen: ack. I'll add mypy tests to ensure async/sync close exist on returned object.

Alex Turner: FYI repro script attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/alex/stream-repro 

Diego Ramos: thumbs up. if we can get this in a patch release next week we avoid more customer hits. :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: moving to triage board. thanks all.
